# Zonorah, Media Neuroscience Lab

> Zonorah is a Media Neuroscience Lab. Our instrument transcribes Peruvian radio, TV and YouTube and measures what is said: open data and applied studies.

Last updated: 2026-11-24

Research on media and the brain. Our computational instrument transcribes Peruvian radio, television and YouTube into a corpus and measures what is said: how much, where, when, by whom and how it is framed.

Before asking what media do to the brain, measure what the media say.

## Method

1. Acquisition. We receive each station's live signal over the internet and record it in the time windows of its schedule.
2. Transcription. A speech-recognition model runs locally and turns audio into timestamped text. Audio is deleted as soon as it is transcribed, so the corpus is text only.
3. Coding. Terms are searched with their variants. Each relevant passage is coded in closed fields: speaker, role of the subject, topic, tone, framing, and evidence or rumour.
4. Output. Figures go to Zonorah Data as minutes on air per 100 hours recorded. Commissioned studies arrive as a PDF by email on the schedule you choose.

## Two fronts, one instrument

Zonorah is a Media Neuroscience Lab. Its computational instrument measures the media side of the question; our research on the brain side is separate and builds on that data.

### Scientific research: Open data on the media side

Published, literal rules, such as the El Niño index, and aggregate open data for journalists, teachers and researchers: a comparator, embeddable charts, CSV downloads and an AI assistant that quotes short fragments with their station and time.

Every figure: minutes on air per 100 hours recorded

### Commercial research: Applied media studies

Organisations define the sources, keywords and rules. Each mention is coded for speaker, topic, tone, framing, evidence or rumour, risk and urgency, and delivered as a PDF study by email.

A commission is private: public data never reveals who asked for what

### Zonorah Data: The lab's open instrument

The comparator contrasts any term across stations, days and regions. A figure is cited with the permanent link of its comparison and the date of consultation.

Cite as: Zonorah (2026). Memoria de los medios del Perú: minutos al aire por cada 100 horas grabadas.

### Method limits: What the figures do not say

Transcription is automatic and errs on names, acronyms and brands, so figures tend to fall short. Only what was recorded is measured, music and adverts count, and figures are rounded.

“Not recorded” is not the same as “not said”

### Data protection: No recordings kept

Audio is deleted as soon as it is transcribed. Questions to the AI assistant go to an AI service (Groq, United States) without email or name. Accounts and their data can be deleted at any time.

Access, correction or deletion: hola@zonorah.com

### Scientific foundations: Computational media neuroscience

Zonorah takes the computational side of media neuroscience, such as the work of the Media Neuroscience Lab at UC Santa Barbara on moral narratives, text mining and large media datasets. The instrument does not do brain imaging or experiments with participants.

https://www.medianeuroscience.org/
